VERSE NOVEL · 1998Autobiography of RedAnne Carson

READ THE LAUREATE

An ancient monster tells a modern life

Autobiography of Red · Anne Carson

Carson recasts Geryon, a monster slain by Herakles, as a red-winged boy growing into desire, hurt and artistic self-knowledge. The book is at once a novel, a poem and a conversation with antiquity.

01

Myth changes viewpoint

The defeated monster becomes the speaking subject, making an old heroic story intimate and morally unsettled.

02

Form follows experience

Verse, narrative and fragment cross their borders because memory and desire do not arrive in one neat genre.

03

Art makes a self

Geryon’s camera and images turn observation into a way to survive, interpret and author his life.

Publisher book page ↗

WHY IT MATTERS

Genres refuse their borders

Carson brings classical scholarship, translation, poetry, essay, performance, and personal experience into forms that cannot be contained by a single literary category.

Verified source ↗
INPUT Classical fragments + lived experience
PROCESS Translation, juxtaposition, genre crossing
OUTPUT New poetic and essayistic forms
